main_body: Palm tree: a drooping frond canopy (about 32px wide, rows 0-22) on a thin brown trunk (about 5px wide, rows 18-54). The canopy is the largest volume.
top_band: Light green crown patch (#71a854, L=142) at rows 2-6 in column x=16, then a dark outline row 7, then the darker drooping fronds below.
evidence: Column x=16 shows a light crown top at rows 2-6 and a 1-row dark edge at row 7. Below that come the darker frond masses (L about 28-55) for roughly 11 rows, then the trunk. The crown is seen from above with the fronds hanging in front, so the canopy reads as 3/4. The trunk is a plain vertical pole, but the canopy is the main body. The light top patch is small, so this is borderline, but it passes.

style.evidence: Only 13 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The canopy has about 4-5 greens in large, simply shaded frond blocks, with no leaf clumps or per-leaf highlights. The trunk is a mechanical 2-row alternating stripe (#4f2e1b / #694026) with almost no grain. The outline is a dark green-tinted tone (only 16% of dark edge pixels are neutral) and is acceptable. Overall it is much thinner and simpler than the lush Beodeul trees.
